# JSON Schema

> Convert Types to JSON Schema and back

# Overview

> Generate JSON Schema from a Type with arktype, or build a Type from JSON Schema with @ark/json-schema.

ArkType converts in both directions, with one package for each.

| direction | package | API |
| - | - | - |
| Type → JSON Schema | `arktype` | `T.toJsonSchema()`, `T["~standard"].jsonSchema` |
| JSON Schema → Type | `@ark/json-schema` | `jsonSchemaToType(schema)` |

## Type to JSON Schema

Every Type has a `toJsonSchema()` method. Nothing else to install:

```ts
const User = type({
	name: "string",
	"age?": "number.integer >= 0"
})

const schema = User.toJsonSchema()
```

```json
{
	"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
	"type": "object",
	"properties": {
		"name": { "type": "string" },
		"age": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }
	},
	"required": ["name"]
}
```

Some things a Type can check, like a `Date`, a `bigint` or a custom `narrow`, have no JSON Schema equivalent. `toJsonSchema()` throws on those unless you tell it what to write instead. See [To JSON Schema](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/to-json-schema).

Libraries that accept any [Standard JSON Schema](https://standardschema.dev/json-schema) read it from `T["~standard"].jsonSchema`, which never throws for those parts. See [Standard JSON Schema](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/to-json-schema#standard-json-schema).

## JSON Schema to Type

`@ark/json-schema` parses a JSON Schema into a Type:

```bash
npm install @ark/json-schema
```

```ts
import { jsonSchemaToType } from "@ark/json-schema"

const User = jsonSchemaToType({
	type: "object",
	properties: {
		name: { type: "string" },
		age: { type: "integer", minimum: 0 }
	},
	required: ["name"]
})

User.expression // "{ name: string, age?: number % 1 & >= 0 }"
// ArkErrors: age must be an integer (was 1.5)
User({ name: "Ada", age: 1.5 })
```

The schema is a runtime value, so the result is a `Type<unknown>`. See [From JSON Schema](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/from-json-schema) to give it a static type, and [Keyword support](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/support) for which keywords it understands.

# To JSON Schema

> Generate a JSON Schema from any Type, pick a draft, and decide what to write for what JSON Schema can't express.

Every Type has a `toJsonSchema()` method:

```ts
const User = type({
	name: "string",
	"age?": "number.integer >= 0"
})

const schema = User.toJsonSchema()
```

```json
{
	"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
	"type": "object",
	"properties": {
		"name": { "type": "string" },
		"age": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }
	},
	"required": ["name"]
}
```

## Options

| option | default | effect |
| - | - | - |
| `target` | `"draft-2020-12"` | the draft to write, `"draft-2020-12"` or `"draft-07"` |
| `dialect` | the target's URL | the `$schema` value. `null` omits it. Takes precedence over `target`'s URL |
| `useRefs` | `false` | write each part once under `$defs` and point to it with `$ref`. Cyclic Types always do |
| `fallback` | throws | what to write for a part JSON Schema can't express. See [Fallbacks](#fallbacks) |

### target

The drafts differ in how they write tuples and where they put definitions:

```ts
const Pair = type(["string", "number"])

Pair.toJsonSchema()
// {
// 	$schema: "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
// 	type: "array",
// 	minItems: 2,
// 	prefixItems: [{ type: "string" }, { type: "number" }],
// 	items: false
// }

Pair.toJsonSchema({ target: "draft-07" })
// {
// 	$schema: "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
// 	type: "array",
// 	minItems: 2,
// 	items: [{ type: "string" }, { type: "number" }],
// 	additionalItems: false
// }
```

`draft-07` writes `definitions` where `draft-2020-12` writes `$defs`.

### dialect

```ts
type("string").toJsonSchema({ dialect: null }) // { type: "string" }
```

### Cyclic types

A cyclic Type is written as a `$ref` to its definition. The definition's name, like `Node1` below, is generated from the alias, so don't rely on it staying the same:

```ts
const types = scope({ Node: { value: "number", "next?": "Node" } }).export()

const schema = types.Node.toJsonSchema()
```

```json
{
	"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
	"$ref": "#/$defs/Node1",
	"$defs": {
		"Node1": {
			"type": "object",
			"properties": {
				"value": { "type": "number" },
				"next": { "$ref": "#/$defs/Node1" }
			},
			"required": ["value"]
		}
	}
}
```

## How Types map

| ArkType | JSON Schema |
| - | - |
| `"string"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"`, `"null"` | `type` |
| `"number.integer"`, `"number % 2"` | `type: "integer"`, plus `multipleOf: 2` |
| `"0 < number <= 1"` | `exclusiveMinimum: 0`, `maximum: 1` |
| `"string >= 1"`, `"string == 2"` | `minLength`, or `minLength` and `maxLength` |
| `"string[] > 0"` | `items`, `minItems: 1` |
| `["string", "number?"]` | `prefixItems`, `minItems: 1`, `items: false` |
| `/^a/` | `pattern: "^a"` |
| `"string.email"` | `pattern`, `format: "email"` |
| `"'a' \| 'b'"` | `enum: ["a", "b"]` |
| `"string \| null"` | `anyOf` |
| `{ "name?": "string" }` | `properties`, with only required keys in `required` |
| `{ "+": "reject", ... }` | `additionalProperties: false` |
| `"Record<string, number>"` | `additionalProperties: {...}` |
| `{ id: "string", "[string]": "string" }` | `patternProperties: { "": {...} }` |
| `{ "[/^x-/]": "string" }` | `patternProperties: { "^x-": {...} }` |
| `{ role: "string = 'user'" }` | `default: "user"` on `role` |
| `.describe("...")`, `.configure({ title, examples })` | `description`, `title`, `examples` |

An index signature applies to every key, including declared ones. JSON Schema skips declared keys in `additionalProperties`, so an index signature next to declared keys is written as `patternProperties` with a pattern every key matches.

## Fallbacks

Some things a Type checks have no JSON Schema equivalent: a `Date`, a `bigint`, a morph, a `narrow`. By default, `toJsonSchema()` throws a `ToJsonSchemaError` for them:

```ts
type({ at: "Date" }).toJsonSchema() // throws ToJsonSchemaError (code "date")
```

Pass a handler for its [code](#fallback-codes) to write something instead. The handler receives the schema written so far as `ctx.base`, plus fields for its code, and returns the schema to use:

```ts
const Event = type({ name: "string", at: "Date" })

const schema = Event.toJsonSchema({
	fallback: {
		date: ctx => ({ ...ctx.base, type: "string", format: "date-time" })
	}
})
```

```json
{
	"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
	"type": "object",
	"properties": {
		"at": { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" },
		"name": { "type": "string" }
	},
	"required": ["at", "name"]
}
```

A `default` handler covers every code you don't list. Passing a function instead of an object is the same as passing it as `default`. Return `ctx.base` to leave out what JSON Schema can't express:

```ts
// properties.at is now {}
Event.toJsonSchema({ fallback: ctx => ctx.base })
```

Leaving something out makes the schema accept values the Type rejects.

For `defaultValue`, `base` is the property's own schema, so returning it makes the schema contain itself. Return `undefined` to drop the default instead, e.g. `{ defaultValue: () => undefined, default: ctx => ctx.base }`.

### Morphs

A morph has a different input and output, so there is no single schema for it. Convert one side with `.in` or `.out`:

```ts
const Tags = type("string")
	.pipe(s => s.split(","))
	.to("string[]")

Tags.in.toJsonSchema() // { $schema: "...", type: "string" }
Tags.out.toJsonSchema() // { $schema: "...", type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }
```

### annotatingFallback

To keep what JSON Schema can't express rather than drop it, pass `annotatingFallback`. It writes each such constraint as an `x-arktype-*` keyword, naming a function, class or symbol by its `$ark` name as a Type's `.json` does:

```ts
import { annotatingFallback, type } from "arktype"

const schema = type({
	id: "bigint",
	createdAt: "Date"
}).toJsonSchema({ fallback: annotatingFallback })
```

```json
{
	"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
	"type": "object",
	"properties": {
		"createdAt": { "x-arktype-proto": "Date" },
		"id": { "x-arktype-domain": "bigint" }
	},
	"required": ["createdAt", "id"]
}
```

Validators ignore those keywords, so the schema still accepts values the Type rejects.

### Fallback codes

Every reason `toJsonSchema()` can throw, with the fields its handler receives besides `code` and `base`:

| code | raised for | example | fields |
| - | - | - | - |
| `arrayObject` | an array with named properties | `type("string[]").and({ n: "number" })` | `object` |
| `arrayPostfix` | elements after a variadic element | `type(["...", "string[]", "number"])` | `elements` |
| `date` | a `Date`, with its bounds | `type("Date")` | `before`, `after` |
| `defaultValue` | a default that isn't JSON. Return `undefined` to omit it | `type({ n: "bigint = 5n" })`, after `domain` | `value` |
| `domain` | `bigint` or `symbol` | `type("bigint")` | `domain` |
| `morph` | a morph | `type("string.trim")` | `out`, the output schema or `null` |
| `patternIntersection` | a second regex on the same string | `type(/^a/).and(/b$/)` | `pattern` |
| `predicate` | a `narrow` | `type("number").narrow(n => n > 0)` | `predicate` |
| `proto` | an `instanceof` other than `Array` or `Date` | `type("Map")` | `proto` |
| `symbolKey` | a symbol key or index signature | `type({ "[symbol]": "string" })` | `key` (`null` for an index), `value`, `optional` |
| `unit` | a literal that isn't JSON | `type("undefined")` | `unit` |

A `Date` is reported as `date`, never `proto`.

## Configuration

`toJsonSchema` options can also be set [globally or on a scope](https://arktype.io/docs/configuration#levels). Options passed to `toJsonSchema()` are merged over them:

```ts
import { configure } from "arktype/config"

configure({
	toJsonSchema: {
		target: "draft-07",
		fallback: {
			date: ctx => ({ ...ctx.base, type: "string", format: "date-time" })
		}
	}
})
```

```ts
// import your config file before arktype
import "./config.ts"
import { type } from "arktype"

// $schema is draft-07's, and at is { type: "string", format: "date-time" }
type({ at: "Date" }).toJsonSchema()
```

A handler passed to `toJsonSchema()` replaces the configured one for its code. A `default` passed there replaces every configured handler.

## Standard JSON Schema

Libraries that accept any [Standard JSON Schema](https://standardschema.dev/json-schema) read a Type's schema from `~standard.jsonSchema`. `input` describes what the Type accepts, `output` what it returns after its morphs:

```ts
const Form = type({
	tags: type("string")
		.pipe(s => s.split(","))
		.to("string[]"),
	"id?": "bigint"
})

// properties: { tags: { type: "string" }, id: {} }
Form["~standard"].jsonSchema.input({ target: "draft-2020-12" })

// properties: { tags: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }, id: {} }
Form["~standard"].jsonSchema.output({ target: "draft-2020-12" })
```

Unlike `toJsonSchema()`, these never throw for a part JSON Schema can't express. They write as much of it as JSON Schema can describe, or `{}` if nothing, so `id` above accepts any value.

- `target` must be `"draft-2020-12"` or `"draft-07"`. Anything else throws.
- `libraryOptions` are passed to `toJsonSchema()` as options, e.g. `{ dialect: null }`.
- Fallback handlers you configure or pass in `libraryOptions` still apply. Only the default throwing handlers are replaced.

# From JSON Schema

> Parse a JSON Schema into a Type with @ark/json-schema and give the result a static type.

```bash
npm install @ark/json-schema
```

`@ark/json-schema` depends on a fixed `arktype` version, not a peer range. If your `arktype` version differs, your package manager installs a second copy.

`jsonSchemaToType` parses a JSON Schema into a Type:

```ts
import { jsonSchemaToType } from "@ark/json-schema"

const User = jsonSchemaToType({
	type: "object",
	properties: {
		name: { type: "string" },
		age: { type: "integer", minimum: 0 }
	},
	required: ["name"]
})

User.expression // "{ name: string, age?: number % 1 & >= 0 }"
User({ name: "Ada" }) // { name: "Ada" }
// ArkErrors: age must be an integer (was 1.5)
User({ name: "Ada", age: 1.5 })
```

`true` parses to `unknown` and `false` to `never`.

## Giving it a type

The schema is a value, so its shape isn't inferred. `jsonSchemaToType` returns a `Type<unknown>`. If you know the shape, cast it with `.as`:

```ts
import { jsonSchemaToType } from "@ark/json-schema"

const User = jsonSchemaToType({
	type: "object",
	properties: { name: { type: "string" } },
	required: ["name"]
}).as<{ name: string }>()

// { name: string }
const user = User.assert({ name: "Ada" })
```

`.as` is not checked against the schema, so keep the two in sync yourself.

## Invalid schemas

`jsonSchemaToType` throws if the schema is malformed or uses a keyword it can't convert:

```ts
// TraversalError: minLength must be non-negative (was -1)
jsonSchemaToType({ type: "string", minLength: -1 })

// ParseError: divisor must be an integer (was 0.5)
jsonSchemaToType({ type: "number", multipleOf: 0.5 })
```

[Keyword support](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/support) lists what throws and what is ignored.

## Typing a schema

A schema written inline in the call is checked against the `JsonSchema` type. To check one you declare separately, use `JsonSchema` from `arktype`:

```ts
import type { JsonSchema } from "arktype"

const Age = {
	type: "integer",
	minimum: 0
} satisfies JsonSchema.Numeric
```

## JsonSchemaScope

`JsonSchemaScope` is the [module](https://arktype.io/docs/scopes) `jsonSchemaToType` validates its input with. Its `ArraySchema`, `NumberSchema`, `ObjectSchema` and `StringSchema` Types check a schema of that kind without converting it:

```ts
import { JsonSchemaScope } from "@ark/json-schema"

// ArkErrors: minimum must be a number (was a string)
JsonSchemaScope.NumberSchema({ type: "number", minimum: "0" })
```

## Back to JSON Schema

A Type from `jsonSchemaToType` has [`toJsonSchema()`](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/to-json-schema) like any other. Keywords it checks with a `narrow`, like `uniqueItems`, `contains`, `oneOf` and `not`, come back as [`predicate` fallbacks](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/to-json-schema#fallback-codes), so `toJsonSchema()` throws for them unless you handle that code.

# Keyword support

> Which JSON Schema keywords @ark/json-schema converts, which throw, and which it ignores.

`jsonSchemaToType` handles each keyword in one of three ways:

- **supported**: the Type checks it.
- **throws**: `jsonSchemaToType` throws a `ParseError` or `TraversalError`.
- **ignored**: the keyword has no effect, so the Type accepts values the schema rejects.

Some ignored keywords, like `if`, `dependentRequired` and `minContains`, are type errors in a schema written inline, since arktype's `JsonSchema` type doesn't include them. A schema loaded at runtime gets no such check.

## Core

| keyword | support | notes |
| - | - | - |
| `true`, `false` | supported | `unknown` and `never` |
| `type` | supported | a single name or an array of names |
| `const`, `enum` | supported | together, they throw. An object or array value is compared by reference, so no parsed value matches it |
| `$ref`, `$dynamicRef` | **throws** | not resolved. Alone, the schema throws. Next to `type`, they are ignored |
| `$defs`, `definitions` | **ignored** | nothing can refer to them |
| `title`, `description`, `default`, `examples`, `deprecated`, `readOnly`, `writeOnly` | **ignored** | not validation keywords. `default` is not applied either |
| `$schema`, `$id`, `$anchor`, `$comment` | **ignored** | |
| `contentEncoding`, `contentMediaType` | **ignored** | |
| `nullable` (OpenAPI) | **ignored** | write `type: ["string", "null"]` instead |

Every schema needs at least one of `type`, `const`, `enum`, `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf` or `not`. Without one it throws, which includes `{}` and subschemas like `{ minimum: 0 }` inside `allOf`.

With an array of names in `type`, keywords for a single type are ignored. `{ type: ["string", "number"], minLength: 2 }` accepts `"a"`. `integer` is the exception: `{ type: ["integer", "null"] }` rejects `1.5`.

## Composition

| keyword | support | notes |
| - | - | - |
| `allOf`, `anyOf` | supported | |
| `oneOf`, `not` | supported | checked with a `narrow` |
| `if`, `then`, `else` | **ignored** | |

Only one composition keyword per schema is used. If a schema has more than one, the first in the order `allOf`, `anyOf`, `not`, `oneOf` is used and the rest are ignored. Nest them in `allOf` to combine them:

```ts
import { jsonSchemaToType } from "@ark/json-schema"

const T = jsonSchemaToType({
	allOf: [
		{ anyOf: [{ type: "string" }, { type: "number" }] },
		{ not: { const: 0 } }
	]
})

// ArkErrors: must be not: 0 (was 0)
T(0)
```

## Strings

| keyword | support | notes |
| - | - | - |
| `minLength`, `maxLength` | supported | |
| `pattern` | supported | |
| `format` | **ignored** | |

## Numbers

| keyword | support | notes |
| - | - | - |
| `minimum`, `maximum` | supported | with `exclusiveMinimum` or `exclusiveMaximum` on the same side, throws |
| `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum` | supported | a number. Draft 4's boolean form throws |
| `multipleOf` | supported | integers only. `0.5` throws |

## Arrays

| keyword | support | notes |
| - | - | - |
| `items` | supported | a schema, a boolean, or an array of schemas (draft 7 tuples) |
| `prefixItems` | supported | with `items`, `items` is the rest. With `items` and `additionalItems`, throws |
| `additionalItems` | supported | after an array of `items`. After a single `items` schema, throws. Alone, it applies to every item, though JSON Schema ignores it there |
| `minItems`, `maxItems` | supported | |
| `uniqueItems` | supported | checked with a `narrow` |
| `contains` | supported | checked with a `narrow` |
| `minContains`, `maxContains` | **ignored** | |
| `unevaluatedItems` | **ignored** | |

## Objects

| keyword | support | notes |
| - | - | - |
| `properties`, `required` | supported | `required` without `properties`, or naming a key not in it, throws |
| `additionalProperties` | supported | `false` rejects other keys. A schema is checked with a `narrow` |
| `patternProperties` | supported | |
| `propertyNames` | supported | keys that don't match are rejected. A `required` key that doesn't match throws |
| `minProperties`, `maxProperties` | supported | checked with a `narrow` |
| `dependentRequired`, `dependentSchemas`, `dependencies` | **ignored** | |
| `unevaluatedProperties` | **ignored** | |

Keywords checked with a `narrow` don't appear in the Type's `expression` and can't be [converted back](https://arktype.io/docs/json-schema/from-json-schema#back-to-json-schema) without a fallback.
